Plattsburg, N. Y. Sept. 1.—Two carloads of elk
from Wyoming, comprising a herd of forty-three
animals, were delivered at Paul Smiths to-day and
will be turned loose in the forest preserve of forty
thousand acres owned by Paul Smith at St. Regis
Lake. The elk are a present to Paul Smith from a
friend in California. The animals arrived in good
condition and will be liberated tomorrow.

Dr. R. Z. Kendall, of Saranac Lake, that he is
about to ship him a carload of elk to be distri-
buted about the Adirondacks wherever he finds
places for them. Dr. Kendall has been active in

big game. Dr. Kendall has decided to release some
of the elk on the State road just above the new
State bridge, Saranac Lake.

dacks in the first week of the open season is far
greater than ever killed at this time of the
year. Many hunting parties have been successful,
and it is said the deer were never so plentiful
before. Some attribute the fact that the deer are
numerous around the backwoods farms to the
destruction of their usual feeding places by forest
fires early in the season. Hardly any field or a
meadow in the woods does not serve as feeding
place for deer.
